discovery: Cavity optomechanics: quantum control of macroscopic mechanical motion with light and microwaves

nominees.name: Markus Aspelmeyer
nominees.affiliation: University of Vienna and IQOQI Vienna, Austria

nominees.name: Tobias J. Kippenberg
nominees.affiliation: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland

nominees.name: John D. Teufel
nominees.affiliation: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Boulder, USA

motivation: Aspelmeyer, Kippenberg and Teufel founded cavity optomechanics and brought it into the quantum regime. Using radiation pressure in optical and superconducting microwave cavities, they demonstrated resolved-sideband cooling of engineered mechanical resonators to their quantum ground state (Teufel 2011; Aspelmeyer, Painter and colleagues 2011). They also achieved strong optomechanical coupling, coherent state transfer between photons and phonons, squeezed light from mechanical motion, and entanglement of mechanical and electromagnetic degrees of freedom. These experiments show that motion of objects containing billions of atoms obeys quantum mechanics and can be controlled at the quantum limit. Optomechanics now underpins quantum-limited force and displacement sensing, microwave-to-optical transduction for networking superconducting quantum processors, and tests of quantum mechanics at macroscopic mass scales. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum effects in electrical circuits. This nomination extends that recognition to mechanical motion, a second macroscopic degree of freedom brought under coherent quantum control.
